info.title: Kudos HTTP API
info.summary: Every route of the Kudos testimonial app, with auth, limits and error shapes.
info.description:
HTTP surface of Kudos, a testimonial collector (Laravel 13 + Inertia 3). Kudos is a server-rendered web app, not a
token API: every page route doubles as a JSON endpoint when you speak the Inertia protocol, and every form route
answers with redirects. This document lists every route the app registers and every response its code can produce.

## Who may call what

| Audience | Routes | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anyone | `/livez`, `/readyz`, `/up`, `/client-logs`, `/{slug}` (GET, POST), `/embed/...`, `/stripe/webhook` | Nothing for GETs. POSTs need the CSRF cookie flow, except `/client-logs` and the webhook. |
| Guests only | `/register`, `/login`, `/forgot-password`, `/reset-password` | No session user. Signed-in users are redirected to `/dashboard`. |
| Signed-in owners | `/logout`, `/settings/*`, `/confirm-password`, `/email/verification-notification`, `/verify-email*` | Session cookie. |
| Verified owners | `/dashboard`, `/spaces*`, `/testimonials/*`, `/billing*` | Session cookie and a verified email. An unverified user is redirected to `/verify-email`. |

There are no API keys or bearer tokens. Authentication is the Laravel session cookie (`kudos_session`, HttpOnly,
SameSite=Lax, 120 minutes). Ownership is checked per record: another owner's space or testimonial gives 403.

## CSRF cookie flow

1. Send any GET (for example `GET /login`). The response sets two cookies: `XSRF-TOKEN` (readable) and `kudos_session`.
2. URL-decode the `XSRF-TOKEN` value and send it as the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header on every `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE`,
   with the same cookie jar.
3. Signing in regenerates the session, so the token changes: read the cookie again after `POST /login`.
4. Exempt: `POST /client-logs` (checked by Origin instead) and `POST /stripe/webhook` (checked by Stripe signature).
5. A missing or wrong token gives `419`.

## Inertia protocol

Page routes return an HTML document by default. Send `X-Inertia: true` and `X-Inertia-Version: <version>` and the same
route returns a JSON page object `{component, props, url, version, sharedProps}` with `Vary: X-Inertia`. Get the version
from the first HTML page (`"version"` inside the `data-page` script) or from any earlier page object.

* A GET with `X-Inertia: true` and a stale or missing version returns `409` with `X-Inertia-Location` (reload the URL).
* Any other failure with `X-Inertia: true` (404, 403, 419, 429, 500) returns an Inertia page object for the component `errors/error` with the real status code (props `status`, `copyKey`, `retryAfter`, `requestId`). Only a dependency outage (503) returns `409` + `X-Inertia-Location`, so the browser loads the database-free outage page in full.
* After `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` an Inertia client gets `303` where others get `302`.
* Flash messages (`props.flash.success`, `props.flash.error`) and validation errors (`props.errors`) of a redirect appear
  once, in the next page object, then vanish.

## Two ways to talk to the form routes

| You send | Success | Validation failure | Unauthenticated | Other failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Accept: application/json` (no X-Inertia) | 302/303 redirect (do not follow it blindly) or 204 | `422` `{message, errors}` | `401` `{message}` | `{error, code, dependency, request_id}` |
| Neither header (plain HTML) | redirect | redirect back | `302` to `/login` | HTML error page |
| `X-Inertia: true` or a browser form post | redirect | redirect back, errors in the next page's `props.errors` | `302` to `/login` | `errors/error` page object with the real status (503: 409 + `X-Inertia-Location`) |

The collections in `docs/api` use the JSON style for error cases and the Inertia style to read page props.

## Error shapes

* `ErrorResponse` `{error, code, dependency, request_id}`: 403, 404, 419, 429, 500, 503. `error` is generic text; use the status.
  `code` is `unavailable` and `dependency` is `database`, `billing` or `app` for a 503; otherwise `error` and `null`.
* `ValidationError` `{message, errors}`: 422.
* `Unauthenticated` `{message}`: 401.
* `EdgeErrorResponse`: like ErrorResponse plus `source: "edge"`, produced by nginx when the app does not answer.

## Headers

* `X-Request-ID`: send your own (8 to 64 chars of `A-Za-z0-9._-`) or get one; it is echoed on every response, including errors.
  `traceparent` (W3C) is also read for log correlation.
* `Retry-After`: on 429 and on every 503 (5 seconds for dependency failures).
* `X-Inertia`, `X-Inertia-Version`, `X-Inertia-Location`: see above.
* `Cache-Control: no-store, private` on error bodies; probes send `no-store`.
* Every response from the app carries `Permissions-Policy` and `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`, plus `Strict-Transport-Security` over HTTPS.
  A nonce-based `Content-Security-Policy` is added when `CSP_ENABLED` is true (default in production only; `CSP_REPORT_ONLY=true` makes it report-only).
  Embed routes get `frame-ancestors *` in it and lose `X-Frame-Options`; every other route has `frame-ancestors 'self'` and, behind nginx, `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`.

## Rate limits

| Route | Limit | Over the limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /login` | 5 failed attempts per email + IP | `422` with the throttle message on `email`, not 429 |
| `POST /{slug}` | 20 per minute | `429` + `Retry-After` |
| `POST /client-logs` | 60 per minute | `429` + `Retry-After` |
| `POST /email/verification-notification`, `GET /verify-email/{id}/{hash}` | 6 per minute | `429` + `Retry-After` |
| Edge nginx: `/login`, `/register`, `/forgot-password`, `/reset-password` | 10 per minute per IP, burst 10 | nginx 503, shown as the edge outage response |
| Edge nginx: `/client-logs` | 5 per second per IP, burst 20, body at most 16 KB | nginx 503 (outage response) or 413 |

The four `throttle:N,1` routes use Laravel's unnamed limiter, whose key is the user id (signed in) or the IP (anonymous),
not the route. They therefore share one counter: 60 log lines in a minute also lock `POST /{slug}` for the rest of that minute.
Verified against the running app.

## Plan limits (Free)

One space, ten testimonials per space. Limits never delete data on downgrade. Hitting them is not an HTTP error:
creating a second space redirects to `/billing` with a flash error, and a full or closed space redirects back from
`POST /{slug}` with a flash error. See the operations for the exact messages.

## Servers

Local dev serves `php artisan serve` on port 8010 (no nginx). The prod-style stack puts nginx in front of php-fpm; run it on
another port with `APP_PORT=8011` to keep dev running. Edge-level responses (outage 503 JSON, `/healthz`, the `limit_req`
zones) exist only there.

servers.description: Local dev stack (docker compose, php artisan serve, no nginx). Demo owner demo@kudos.test / password is local seed data.
Prod-style stack (docker-compose.prod.yml, nginx edge in front of php-fpm) published with APP_PORT=8011.
Edge in front of a real deployment (TLS terminated by your proxy). The `edge` 503 JSON appears here.

tags.description: Routes that exist but are not product API: home page, Laravel health check, local storage, dev-only Inertia devtools.

get.description: Answers 200 as long as PHP runs. No database read, no session.

200.description: Alive.

get.description: Checks the database (critical), the cache and the public storage disk (both informational). 503 only when a critical check fails. Used by the edge and orchestrators.

200.description: Ready. A non-critical check can still be `up: false` here.

get.description: Framework route registered by `withRouting(health: '/up')`. Returns the app's own status and fires the DiagnosingHealth event. Prefer /livez and /readyz.

200.description: Up.

post.description: Used by `resources/js/lib/logger.ts` (often through `navigator.sendBeacon`). Open endpoint: no session, no CSRF (a beacon cannot carry the token), so it only takes same-origin browser requests. If a `Sec-Fetch-Site` header is present it must be `same-origin` or `none`; otherwise an `Origin` header is required and its host must equal the request host. A request with neither header (a plain script) is refused with 403. Authorization is checked before validation, so a refused request never gets a 422. Limits: `throttle:60,1` in the app (shared bucket), and at the edge 5 requests per second with a burst of 20 and a 16 KB body cap. At most 20 lines per request, each `data` object at most 4000 bytes of JSON. Never put secrets or full bodies in `data`; the logger redacts keys such as password and token.
post.x-rate-limit: 60 requests per minute (shared bucket, see TooManyRequests)

get.description: The page a respondent opens. `props.accepting` is false when the owner switched the form off, or when the owner is on Free and the space already holds 10 testimonials; the form should then be hidden. Unknown or reserved slugs give 404. Public: no login.

post.description:
Creates a testimonial with status `pending`. Public, but the CSRF cookie flow still applies (any anonymous page view sets it). Limit: `throttle:20,1`, enforced before validation, so invalid posts count too. Optional fields are validated against the space's field configuration. HTML tags in text fields are stripped. Photo upload needs `multipart/form-data`.

Free plan: a space accepts at most 10 testimonials while its owner has no subscription. Past that, or when the owner switched the form off, nothing is stored and the response is a redirect back with `flash.error` = "This space is not accepting testimonials right now." (not a 4xx). Existing data is never deleted on downgrade.

302.description: Back to the previous page (Referer, or the last visited URL). On success `flash.success` = "Thank you! Your testimonial was sent."; when the plan limit or the closed form stopped it, `flash.error` is set instead. Nothing in the status tells these apart: read the flash on the next page load.

get.description: HTML page listing the published testimonials of a space, meant for `<iframe src="…/embed/{spaceId}">`. Sends `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors *` and drops X-Frame-Options, so any site can frame it. Never contains respondent emails. Not rate limited; do not poll it, use the JSON route with your own cache.

200.description: Page. The HTML document by default; the Inertia page object as JSON with `X-Inertia: true`.

get.description: Same data as the wall, for custom rendering. Published testimonials only. Fields: no email, no status, no favorite flag. CORS headers are not sent, so browsers on other origins cannot read this response from script; use the iframe, or fetch it server-side.

200.description: Published testimonials.

get.description: Inertia page `auth/register`. Signed-in users are redirected to /dashboard.

200.description: Page. The HTML document by default; the Inertia page object as JSON with `X-Inertia: true`.

post.description: Creates the user, fires the Registered event (verification mail), signs the user in and redirects to /dashboard. Free plan applies from the start. Verification is required before dashboard, spaces and billing (middleware `verified`).

302.description: Success: to /dashboard (signed in). Already signed in: also /dashboard.

get.description: Inertia page `auth/login`. This is also the easiest way to get the XSRF-TOKEN cookie, the session cookie and the Inertia asset version.

200.description: Page. The HTML document by default; the Inertia page object as JSON with `X-Inertia: true`.

post.description: Checks the credentials, regenerates the session id (so the CSRF token changes: read the new XSRF-TOKEN cookie afterwards) and redirects to the URL the user tried to open, else /dashboard. Limit: 5 failed attempts per email + IP, then 422 with the throttle message (this is not a 429). The edge nginx also limits /login, /register, /forgot-password and /reset-password to 10 requests/minute per IP with a burst of 10 (excess requests get nginx's default limit_req status 503, which the edge's error_page then turns into the outage response with `source: edge`; it is not a 429).

302.description: Success: to the intended URL or /dashboard, session cookie rotated.

post.x-rate-limit: 5 failed attempts per email+IP (422), 10/min per IP at the edge

post.description: Ends the session, rotates the CSRF token and redirects to `/`.

get.description: Inertia page `auth/forgot-password`.

200.description: Page. The HTML document by default; the Inertia page object as JSON with `X-Inertia: true`.

post.description: Always answers the same way for a valid address, whether or not the account exists (`flash`/`status` = "A reset link will be sent if the account exists."). The mail goes to Mailpit in dev.

302.description: Back to the previous page with `props.status`.

get.description: Inertia page `auth/reset-password`; props `token` and `email` echo the URL.

200.description: Page. The HTML document by default; the Inertia page object as JSON with `X-Inertia: true`.

post.summary: Set a new password with a reset token
post.description: Success redirects to /login with `status`. A bad or expired token is reported on the `email` field.

get.description: Inertia page `auth/verify-email` for users whose address is not verified. Verified users are redirected to /dashboard.

200.description: Page. The HTML document by default; the Inertia page object as JSON with `X-Inertia: true`.

get.description: Target of the link in the verification mail. Needs a signed URL (`signed` middleware: bad or expired signature gives 403) and a signed-in user whose id and hash match. Limit `throttle:6,1`. Redirects to /dashboard?verified=1.

post.description: Limit `throttle:6,1` (shared bucket). Already-verified users are redirected to /dashboard without a mail.

302.description: Back with `status` = `verification-link-sent`, or to /dashboard when already verified.

get.description: Inertia page `auth/confirm-password`.

200.description: Page. The HTML document by default; the Inertia page object as JSON with `X-Inertia: true`.

post.description: Stores `auth.password_confirmed_at` in the session and redirects to the intended URL or /dashboard.

get.description: A framework redirect route for every method. Answers 302 with the relative `Location: settings/profile`.
Inertia page `settings/profile`.

200.description: Page. The HTML document by default; the Inertia page object as JSON with `X-Inertia: true`.

patch.description: Changing the email clears `email_verified_at`; the user must verify again before reaching dashboard, spaces or billing.

delete.description: Requires the current password. Signs the user out, deletes the user and redirects to `/`. Destructive: the collection never calls it with the right password.

get.description: Inertia page `settings/password`.

200.description: Page. The HTML document by default; the Inertia page object as JSON with `X-Inertia: true`.

put.description: Needs the current password and a confirmed new one (min 8).

get.description: Inertia page `settings/appearance` (theme choice is stored in the browser).

200.description: Page. The HTML document by default; the Inertia page object as JSON with `X-Inertia: true`.

get.description: Needs a verified email. Prop `stats`: totals, plan usage, a per-day series for the range, and `show_upgrade_banner` (Free plan and not dismissed). An invalid `range` is a validation error (422 as JSON, redirect with flashed error otherwise).

200.description: Page. The HTML document by default; the Inertia page object as JSON with `X-Inertia: true`.

post.description: Sets `banner_dismissed_at` on the user. Permanent; there is no HTTP way to undo it.

get.description: Inertia page `spaces/index`: `spaces` (with `testimonials_count`) and `canCreate` (false on Free once one space exists).

200.description: Page. The HTML document by default; the Inertia page object as JSON with `X-Inertia: true`.

post.description: Free plan: one space. A second create does not return an error status: it redirects to /billing and flashes "Your Free plan includes 1 space. Upgrade to Pro to create more." Success redirects to /spaces/{spaceId} and flashes "Space created. Share its link to collect testimonials." Read the new id from the Location header. The slug is generated from the name (made unique, never a reserved word).

get.description: Inertia page `spaces/form` with `space: null`, `themes` and `optionalFields`. On Free with a space already present it redirects to /billing with the limit message.

200.description: Page. The HTML document by default; the Inertia page object as JSON with `X-Inertia: true`.

get.description: Inertia page `spaces/show`: the space, paginated testimonials (15 per page, newest first, with respondent email), `counts` per filter, the applied `filter` and `range`, and `publicUrl`. Owner only: another owner's space is 403, an unknown id 404.

200.description: Page. The HTML document by default; the Inertia page object as JSON with `X-Inertia: true`.

flash.success: Space created. Share its link to collect testimonials.

put.description: Full update (all required fields again). `PATCH` is an alias with the same rules. Redirects to the inbox. Multipart bodies need `_method=PUT` in a POST.

patch.description: Same handler and rules as PUT: every required field must be sent.

delete.description: Deletes the space and its testimonials. Owner only. Redirects to /spaces with `flash.success` = "Space deleted." The Free-plan slot is free again.

get.description: Inertia page `spaces/form` with the space filled in. Owner only.

200.description: Page. The HTML document by default; the Inertia page object as JSON with `X-Inertia: true`.

patch.description: Owner only. Sets the body (HTML stripped). Redirects back to the inbox.
Owner only. `published` makes it appear in the embed wall; `hidden` removes it; `pending` returns it to the queue.

302.description: Back with `flash.success` = "Status changed to published." (303 for Inertia).

patch.description: Owner only. No body. Flips `is_favorite`; calling twice restores the original value.

get.description: Inertia page `billing/show`; prop `overview` has the plan, usage, subscription status and whether Stripe is configured.

200.description: Page. The HTML document by default; the Inertia page object as JSON with `X-Inertia: true`.

post.description: Builds a Checkout session for the Pro price and sends the browser to Stripe: a plain request gets 302 to checkout.stripe.com, an Inertia request gets 409 + X-Inertia-Location (the Inertia location trick). Already Pro: redirect to /billing, flash "You are already on the Pro plan." Stripe not configured (no STRIPE_SECRET / STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID): redirect to /billing with a generic `flash.error` (the missing setting is only logged). Stripe unreachable after retries: redirect to /billing with "Billing is temporarily unavailable. Nothing was charged. Try again in a moment."

409.description: Inertia request: X-Inertia-Location is the Stripe Checkout URL.

get.description: Stripe sends the browser here after payment with `?session_id=cs_...`. The redirect alone proves nothing: the app asks Stripe whether the session belongs to this user and is complete, then reports. The Pro plan itself turns on when the signed webhook arrives. Always redirects to /billing: `flash.success` ("Welcome to Pro! Your upgrade is active." or "Payment confirmed. Your Pro plan activates as soon as Stripe notifies us ...") or `flash.error` ("We could not confirm that payment." for a missing or foreign session id).

post.description: Needs a Stripe customer. Without one: redirect to /billing with "No billing profile yet." Otherwise 302 to the portal URL (409 + X-Inertia-Location for Inertia clients).

302.description: To the Stripe portal, or to /billing with `flash.error`.

409.description: Inertia request: X-Inertia-Location is the portal URL.

post.description:
Called by Stripe, not by clients. No session, no CSRF (exempt). Cashier verifies the `Stripe-Signature` header against STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and answers 403 for a bad signature. With no secret configured (local default) the check is skipped. Handles customer.subscription.* , invoice and payment events; unknown event types answer 200 and do nothing. Subscription events are what switch a user between Free and Pro.

Local testing: `docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml --profile billing up stripe` forwards real test-mode events here.

200.description: Event accepted (or ignored).

403.description: Signature check failed (only when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set).

value.error: Something went wrong. Please try again.

get.description: Page Cashier uses for off-session payment confirmation (3-D Secure). Not used by the Kudos UI. Behind Cashier's VerifyRedirectUrl middleware. Needs Stripe keys; without them the app answers 500 (a stack trace when APP_DEBUG=true).

200.description: Payment page.

get.description: Inertia page `welcome`. Public.

200.description: Page. The HTML document by default; the Inertia page object as JSON with `X-Inertia: true`.

get.description: Laravel's `storage.local` route. Uploaded logos and photos are served from `public/storage` (a symlink) by the web server first; this route is the fallback of the `local` disk and answers 403 for paths it does not serve.

200.description: File contents.

put.description: Laravel's `storage.local.upload` route for signed temporary upload URLs. Not used by Kudos.

get.description: Registered by the Inertia devtools package. Gated by its own Authorize middleware: local environment only. Do not rely on it.

200.description: Recorded entries.

get.description: One recorded entry. Same gating as the list.

200.description: Entry.

sessionCookie.name: kudos_session
sessionCookie.description: Laravel session cookie set by `POST /login` (and by any first GET, as an anonymous session). Send it back on every request; a cookie jar does this for you.

csrfToken.name: X-XSRF-TOKEN
csrfToken.description: URL-decoded value of the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie. Required together with the session cookie on state-changing requests.

error.description: Human-readable summary. Generic by design; branch on the HTTP status and `code`, not on this text.

code.description: `unavailable` for a failed dependency (503), `error` for everything else.

oneOf.description: Which dependency failed; null unless the status is 503. `app` only in the nginx edge body.

request_id.description: Same value as the X-Request-ID response header. Quote it when reporting a problem.

ErrorResponse.description: Error body for every failure the framework does not already shape, returned when the client sends `Accept: application/json` (and no X-Inertia header).

source.description: Present only when nginx, not the Laravel app, produced the response.

EdgeErrorResponse.description: 503 produced by the edge nginx when the app does not answer (502, 503 and 504 from php-fpm all become this).

message.description: First validation message, plus `(and N more errors)` when there are several.

errors.description: Field name (dotted for nested fields) mapped to its messages.

ValidationError.description: Laravel validation failure, returned as 422 when the client sends `Accept: application/json`.

Unauthenticated.description: 401 body from the auth middleware. This one is Laravel's own shape, not ErrorResponse.

SpaceFields.description: Per-field configuration for the optional fields. Name and email are always required and are not listed.

respondent_email.description: Owner-only. Never present in embed or public output.

body.description: Text with HTML tags already stripped on submit.

EmbedTestimonial.description: Public view of a published testimonial. No email field exists here.

EmbedWall.description: Published testimonials of one space, newest first as the app orders them.

subscription_status.description: `none` when the user never subscribed; otherwise the Cashier subscription status.

Flash.description: One-shot messages from the previous redirect. Read once, then gone.

errors.description: Validation errors flashed by the previous redirect (first message per field).

oneOf.description: The User model: id, name, email, email_verified_at, created_at, updated_at, banner_dismissed_at, stripe_id, pm_type, pm_last_four, trial_ends_at.

SharedProps.description: Props the server adds to every Inertia page. Each page adds its own props next to these.

status.description: The real HTTP status of the response.

copyKey.description: Which wording the React error page shows.

InertiaErrorPage.description: What an Inertia request (X-Inertia: true) receives for a 403, 404, 419, 429, other 4xx or 500: a page object for the component `errors/error`, with the real status code on the response. Unlike normal pages it carries only its own props, no shared props.

component.description: Name of the React page component, for example `spaces/show`.

url.description: Path and query of the page.

version.description: Asset version. Send it back as X-Inertia-Version on GET visits.

InertiaPage.description: Page object that every Inertia route returns when the request carries `X-Inertia: true`.

remember.description: Keep the session after the browser closes.

email.description: Lowercase. Changing it clears email verification.

is_accepting.description: Turn the public form on or off.

logo.description: PNG, JPG, JPEG or WEBP, at most 2 MB. Only valid in multipart bodies. Send `_method=PUT` in a multipart POST to update.

SpaceRequest.description: Create or update a space. In multipart or form bodies use bracket names such as `fields[company][enabled]=1`. The slug is generated from the name and stays the same on update, so shared links keep working. A body replaces the whole configuration: an omitted `collect_rating` becomes false, an omitted `is_accepting` becomes true, an omitted entry in `fields` becomes disabled and not required.

email.description: Validated with the RFC rule. Stored, shown to the owner only.

body.description: HTML tags are stripped before saving.

rating.description: Required when the space collects ratings; prohibited (422) when it does not.

company.description: Allowed only when enabled on the space; required when marked required.

social_link.description: http or https URL. Same enabled/required rule.

photo.description: PNG, JPG, JPEG or WEBP, at most 2 MB. Multipart only. Same enabled/required rule.

SubmissionRequest.description: Respondent submission. Fields the space has not enabled are rejected with `The <field> field is prohibited.`

HtmlDocument.description: HTML document. Inertia pages embed their page object in a script element with the attribute data-page="app" and type application/json.

accepting.description: False when the owner closed the form or the Free plan's 10-testimonial cap is reached.

SpaceId.name: spaceId
SpaceId.description: Space public ID (lowercase ULID). Numeric database ids are never used.

schema.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Reserved names (login, register, dashboard, settings, embed, billing, spaces, stripe, up, livez, readyz, healthz, status, outage, client-logs, forgot-password, reset-password, verify-email, confirm-password, logout, email, testimonials, build, storage) never match this route.

XInertia.name: X-Inertia
XInertia.description: Send `true` to receive the page object as JSON instead of the HTML document. GET requests with this header must also send X-Inertia-Version.

XInertiaVersion.name: X-Inertia-Version
XInertiaVersion.description: Asset version from the last page object (also in the HTML's `data-page` script). A mismatch on GET returns 409 with X-Inertia-Location.

XRequestId.name: X-Request-ID
XRequestId.description: Your own correlation id. Used as the request id when it matches the pattern, otherwise the server generates one. It is echoed in the response.

XXsrfToken.name: X-XSRF-TOKEN
XXsrfToken.description: URL-decoded value of the XSRF-TOKEN cookie. Required on every state-changing request except /client-logs and /stripe/webhook; missing or wrong gives 419.

Referer.name: Referer
Referer.description: Where `back()` redirects go. Without it the app redirects to the last page this session visited, which is rarely what a script wants.

InboxTo.name: to
InboxTo.description: Latest submission date. Must be on or after `from`.

VerifyId.name: id
VerifyId.description: User id from the signed link in the verification email.

VerifyHash.name: hash
VerifyHash.description: SHA-1 of the user's email, from the signed link.

InertiaConflict.description: Inertia location trick: 409 with an empty body and X-Inertia-Location, meaning "load this URL as a normal page". Used when (1) a GET visit sends a stale or missing X-Inertia-Version (after authentication has passed), (2) a dependency outage (503) hits an Inertia request: the full-page load then shows the database-free outage page (for an unsafe method the location is `/`), and (3) billing checkout and portal send the browser to Stripe.

LoginRedirect.description: Browser or Inertia request without a session: 302 to `/login`. The target is remembered and used after sign-in.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit reached. Retry-After holds the seconds to wait. Counters of unnamed `throttle:N,1` routes (`/{slug}` POST, /client-logs, /email/verification-notification, /verify-email/...) share one bucket per user (signed in) or per IP (anonymous), so traffic to one of them can lock out the others. Same body variants as 403.

Unavailable.description: A dependency is down (database, Stripe, or the whole app behind nginx). Always carries Retry-After (5 seconds by default). Database and billing failures come from the app; `source: edge` bodies come from nginx. HTML clients get the friendly page, or the static outage page when the edge answered. Inertia requests do not get this status: they get 409 + X-Inertia-Location (see InertiaConflict) so the outage page loads in full.

billing.summary: Stripe retries exhausted or not configured
